messages:
Elena: Heads-up: enterprise customer (ACME) reported duplicate charges after upgrading python SDK from 1.18 -> 1.21. They then pinned to 1.19 and still saw duplicates for a short window before rolling back to 1.18 and the issue stopped.
Elena: Short summary: client retried a call, server accepted two separate requests and both were billed. Customer wasn't setting an explicit idempotency_key. Logs attached (sanitized).
Sam: Yikes. Any changes to client retry/idempotency behavior around 1.20? @Tim can you confirm?
Tim: Yes. In 1.20 we changed the default idempotency token generation and enabled a client-side retry wrapper for generator endpoints on 5xx/network errors. If the retry uses a different idempotency token the server will treat it as a new request.
Elena: Customer says server traces show two different idempotency header values for the retried attempts.
Sam: That would explain double billing. Do we still expose the old idempotency param name? I remember there was a rename.
Tim: We renamed `idempotency` -> `idempotency_key` in 1.20 and made it optional. But the generator that emits the default token was changed to include a timestamp shard, which made retries inconsistent.
Elena: Repro snippet from customer (sanitized):
```
from redwood import Client
c = Client(api_key="REDACTED")
for _ in range(100):
    resp = c.generate("gpt-3-like", prompt="hi")
    # hot loop; network blips cause client-side retry
```
Elena: Logs: client shows one retry, server has two accepted request IDs; billing shows two charges.
Sam: Immediate mitigation suggestions: 1) pin to 1.18, 2) set an explicit idempotency_key per call, or 3) set an env flag to force old generator behavior if available.
Tim: We left an internal env var `RW_IDEMPOTENCY_STABLE=true` for testing but it was not publicized. It will force the 1.18 token generation algorithm. Not ideal to tell customers to rely on internal flags, but it's a short-term fix.
Elena: Customer asked if there's a config knob in 1.21 to restore old behavior.
Sam: Not officially. For now advise explicit idempotency_key or revert to 1.18. We'll ship a hotfix.
billing-bot: Billing records: duplicate charges for ACME on 2025-11-02 13:04 UTC (tx_abc123, tx_def456).
Elena: Escalating to eng-py and billing for refund coordination. Severity: high.
eng-py-bot: Created issue #4321 (idempotency: restore stable generation behind flag) and draft hotfix 1.21.1. Assigned @Sam @Tim.
Sam: I'll open a PR to put the old generator behind a runtime flag and publish 1.21.1. Also add clear release notes calling this out as a breaking change.
Tim: We should add an infra test to assert that retries reuse the same idempotency token when triggered by the client retry wrapper.
Elena: Proposed repro doc to verify fix: 1) run concurrent loop (10+ threads) calling generate; 2) simulate network drops (tc/netem or kill connection); 3) log client-side idempotency header and server request-id; 4) confirm only one accepted request when explicit key is used or hotfix applied.
Sam: I'll post a small asyncio/httpx repro gist and attach to the issue.
Elena: For now telling ACME to pin to 1.18 or set explicit idempotency_key per request. Offering to provide a signed wheel if they need a quick rollback.
Sam: Ping me if they want a temporary package. I'll also prepare the changelog and customer-facing advisory for the support KB.
Tim: After the patch and hotfix publish, we'll follow up with a postmortem and update the SDK docs so idempotency behavior is explicit in the migration notes.
Elena: Thanks team — updating customer and billing. Will follow up here with PR/release links. :thumbsup:
